titulo: Phrasal Verbs, Collocation and Register Shift
descripcion: Choosing between look into, investigate and conduct an inquiry is not really three separate vocabulary choices — it's one skill: reading the register the situation calls for and picking the phrasal verb, its Latinate synonym, or the fixed collocation that fits. Learned as isolated words, these three options compete uselessly; learned as a register ladder, they become one tool.

filas: We need to look into this.
We need to conduct an inquiry into this.

ejemplos.texto: We should look into it before we decide anything.
The board agreed to investigate the matter further.
The company has launched a formal inquiry into the incident.

notas: The three forms are not interchangeable by meaning alone — they signal who is speaking and in what context, which matters as much as the content.
A formal collocation (conduct an inquiry, launch an investigation) usually pairs a specific verb with a specific noun; these pairings are fixed.
Switching from a phrasal verb to a formal collocation mid-paragraph, without reason, reads as inconsistent register.

es.en: Spanish lacks the same triple system of phrasal verb, Latinate verb and fixed collocation, and often uses a single verb («investigar») across registers. Spanish speakers tend to use only the neutral form in English (investigate) and exploit neither the informal nor the institutional end.
es.es: El español no tiene el mismo sistema triple de «phrasal verb», verbo latino y colocación fija, y a menudo usa un único verbo («investigar») en distintos registros. Los hispanohablantes tienden a usar solo la forma neutra en inglés («investigate») y no explotan ni el extremo informal ni el institucional.

de.en: German has its own three-step ladder: «nachschauen» (look into), «untersuchen» (investigate) and «eine Untersuchung durchführen» (conduct an inquiry), including a functional verb construction at the institutional end. German speakers therefore understand the skill intuitively; the work lies in learning the English members of each ladder.
de.de: Im Deutschen gibt es eine eigene dreistufige Leiter: «nachschauen» («look into»), «untersuchen» («investigate») und «eine Untersuchung durchführen» («conduct an inquiry»), einschließlich einer Funktionsverbverbindung am institutionellen Ende. Deutschsprachige verstehen die Fertigkeit daher intuitiv; gelernt werden müssen vor allem die englischen Mitglieder jeder Stufe.

it.en: Italian has the neutral and institutional ends («investigare, condurre un'indagine»), and the informal end mostly in fixed phrases («dare un'occhiata»). Italian speakers therefore use the Latinate verb and the collocation comfortably but rarely reach for the phrasal verb.
it.it: L'italiano possiede gli estremi neutro e istituzionale («investigare», «condurre un'indagine») e il polo informale soprattutto in espressioni fisse («dare un'occhiata»). Gli italofoni usano quindi con facilità il verbo latino e la collocazione, ma ricorrono raramente al «phrasal verb».

fr.en: French has «enquêter» and «mener une enquête» for the neutral and institutional ends, and informal expressions such as «jeter un œil». Like other Romance speakers, French speakers are comfortable with the Latinate verb and the collocation but rarely use the phrasal verb.
fr.fr: Le français a «enquêter» et «mener une enquête» pour les extrêmes neutre et institutionnel, ainsi que des expressions informelles comme «jeter un œil». Comme les autres locuteurs romans, les francophones sont à l'aise avec le verbe latin et la collocation, mais emploient rarement le «phrasal verb».

pt.en: Portuguese has «investigar» and «levar a cabo uma investigação» for the neutral and institutional ends, and informal phrases such as «dar uma olhada». Portuguese speakers therefore use the Latinate verb and the collocation easily but rarely the phrasal verb.
pt.pt: O português tem «investigar» e «levar a cabo uma investigação» para os extremos neutro e institucional, e expressões informais como «dar uma olhada». Falantes de português usam facilmente o verbo latino e a colocação, mas raramente recorrem ao «phrasal verb».

errores: Using only the neutral Latinate verb and never the phrasal or the fixed collocation, missing the full register range.
Mixing an informal phrasal verb with a very formal fixed collocation in the same sentence.
Getting the collocation wrong: conduct an investigation rather than make an investigation.

autochequeo: Does the chosen form (phrasal, neutral, formal) match the register of the whole text?
Is the fixed collocation used with its correct verb, not a substitute?
Have I avoided switching registers mid-paragraph without reason?
Have I used at least two of the three registers deliberately, to show contrast?
Would the intended reader find the register appropriate?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the choice between phrasal verbs, neutral verbs and formal collocations. Check register consistency throughout and flag any incorrect fixed collocation. Do not rewrite the text.

es: «*realizar una investigación*» rendered as *realise an investigation* instead of *conduct an investigation*.
de: «*ein Foto machen*» rendered as *make a photo* instead of *take a photo*.
it: «*fare una domanda*» rendered as *make a question* instead of *ask a question*.
fr: «*passer un examen*» rendered as *pass an exam* when *take* or *sit an exam* is meant.
pt: «*fazer uma pergunta*» rendered as *make a question* instead of *ask a question*.
